questions.question: What is the primary guideline stated in the 'First Rule of ARIA'?
options: Always replace native HTML elements with custom ARIA divs
Use native HTML5 semantic elements whenever possible before adding ARIA roles
ARIA is mandatory on every HTML tag
questions.explanation: The first rule of ARIA specifies that native HTML elements (like <button>) should always be used over re-purposed divs with ARIA.

questions.question: Which attribute provides an accessible text description for a button that contains only a visual icon?
questions.explanation: aria-label provides an accessible string name for an element that has no visible text content.

questions.question: What does aria-hidden="true" tell assistive technologies like screen readers?
options: Highlight the element in bright yellow
Ignore and skip this element and its children in the accessibility tree
questions.hint: It hides the element from the accessibility tree.
questions.explanation: aria-hidden="true" removes the element and all its children from the accessibility tree, making it invisible to screen readers.

questions.question: Which attribute communicates whether a collapsible menu or accordion drawer is currently open or closed?
questions.explanation: aria-expanded indicates whether the interactive widget is expanded (true) or collapsed (false).

questions.question: What are the four core principles of the WCAG accessibility standard (POUR)?
questions.explanation: The four foundational principles of WCAG are Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, and Robust.
